_comment: temper-quality-oracle's expected-failure manifest, the sibling of
wasm_expected_failures.json (temper-drc-rs), wasm_expected_failures_geometry.json,
wasm_expected_failures_thermal.json, wasm_expected_failures_router_core.json,
wasm_expected_failures_design_bundle.json and
wasm_expected_failures_constraint_compiler.json. Same contract -- see
wasm_expected_failures.json's _comment for why divergences are LISTED and executed
rather than deleted or cfg'd out.
It is a separate file rather than more entries in a shared one because
run_wasm_tests.mjs exits non-zero on an ORPHAN EXCLUSION: a manifest entry naming no
registered test. Point the runner at this one with
`--expected-failures tools/wasm/wasm_expected_failures_quality_oracle.json` when the
module carries temper-quality-oracle alone.
Native baseline, for contrast: `cargo test --manifest-path
packages/temper-quality-oracle/Cargo.toml` runs 166 tests and passes 165 on
x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu. The one native failure
(placement_metrics::tests::py_pow_resolves_to_host_libm_not_sqrt) predates this
registration -- it is identical on the base commit -- and is NOT a wasm32 divergence;
see the coverage caveat below.
Measured 2026-08-10 against 126 registered tests: 125 execute, 125 pass, 0
expected-fail, 0 other. The 126th is registered but not executable -- see below.
THIS FILE IS EMPTY, AND THAT IS A RESULT RATHER THAN AN OMISSION.
An empty manifest is NOT a weaker gate. run_wasm_tests.mjs still fails the run on any
unexpected failure, so with nothing excluded here every one of the 125 executable
tests is load-bearing: a regression on wasm32 turns the step red immediately.
None of the established divergence classes has anything to attach to. What survives
`--no-default-features` here is the six-layer quality pipeline -- net classification,
constraint derivation, config assembly, threshold evaluation, the pass/fail oracle,
and the placement / aesthetic / routing / validation scorers. It reads no clock
(no Instant::now, no SystemTime), draws no entropy, touches no filesystem and spawns
no threads: `grep -rn 'Instant::now\|SystemTime\|rand::\|std::fs\|std::thread'
packages/temper-quality-oracle/src/` is empty.
The one place a host facility IS reached -- the `dlsym` libm surface -- the crate
already handles at the source, which is why it produces no entry here. See the
registered-but-not-executable note next.
placement_metrics::tests::py_pow_resolves_to_host_libm_not_sqrt carries its own
`#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]`, so it is NAMED by the registry (the generator
repeats a test's own cfgs on its entry) but the entry is compiled out of a wasm32
build. It never runs, so it can neither pass nor fail, and an entry here would be an
orphan exclusion.
It is the b7-pow class that temper-thermal catalogues with four entries and
temper-drc-rs with three, arrived at from the other direction. This crate resolves
CPython's libm `pow` through `dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT, "pow")` (placement_metrics.rs) and
`log` the same way (aesthetic.rs), because CPython's `x ** 2` is `pow(x, 2.0)` and NOT
`x * x`. wasm32-unknown-unknown has no dynamic loader, so both modules already gate
the dlsym path on `not(target_arch = "wasm32")` and fall back to the std intrinsics.
That anti-vacuity test asserts the divergence is still observable, which it is not
under the fallback -- and the crate had already excluded it in source rather than
letting it fail. Nothing was excluded here to make a number look clean.
--- Coverage caveat, recorded rather than hidden ---------------------------
Because py_pow/py_log fall back to `f64::powf` / `f64::ln` on wasm32, the 26
placement_metrics and 10 aesthetic tests that reach them are exercising a DIFFERENT
libm on this target than natively. They all pass, which means their assertions do not
discriminate between the two -- they pin plumbing and structural properties, not the
last ulp. So the wasm32 tier proves those kernels correct, but it does not re-prove
the bit-for-bit CPython agreement that is this crate's actual contract; only the
native run and the Python differential suite do that. That is a limit of the tier for
this crate, not a defect in these tests, and it is written down here so a reader does
not over-read a green wasm32 run.
Related, and the reason the native baseline is 165/166 rather than 166/166:
py_pow_resolves_to_host_libm_not_sqrt currently FAILS on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu on
this machine, on the base commit as well as on this branch, so it is out of scope for
a registration-only PR. It is the anti-vacuity guard for the whole dlsym mechanism, so
a native failure means the host-libm pow is not actually being reached (or agrees with
sqrt on the pinned operands) -- worth its own investigation, reported rather than
fixed here.
